responsibility.value: Builds and signs the JWT access token for an authenticated user, encoding user id, username, a unique jti, and role claims, using HMAC-SHA256 and config-driven issuer/audience/expiration.

Owns: Claim assembly: sub (userId), unique_name (username), jti (new GUID), one ClaimTypes.Role claim per role
Signing: HMAC-SHA256 using the symmetric key from Jwt:Key config
doesNotOwn: Token validation — this class only issues tokens, does not validate incoming ones
Key management/rotation — Jwt:Key is read as-is from configuration with no rotation or versioning support
Revocation — handled entirely by ITokenRevocationService using the jti this class embeds

collaborators.detail: Sole source of expiration time, keeping the class testable without wall-clock dependency

contracts: Every generated token has a unique jti (fresh GUID per call), which is what makes per-token revocation possible downstream.
assumptions: Jwt:Key is present, non-null, and long enough for HMAC-SHA256 (>= 256 bits) — there is no length validation; a short key degrades security silently rather than failing fast.
The caller passes a non-null roles list — a null list throws NullReferenceException in the claims loop, there is no guard.
Jwt:Issuer / Jwt:Audience being absent produces a token with null issuer/audience; this class does not fail on that, though downstream validation likely would.
failureModes: ArgumentNullException if Jwt:Key is missing from configuration (the null-forgiving `!` operator suppresses the compiler warning, not the runtime failure)
architecturalNotes: No startup-time validation of Jwt:Key presence/length exists in this class — if that validation exists elsewhere (e.g. options validation at startup), this is fine; if not, a misconfigured deployment fails at first login rather than at boot.
